messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

facilities.description: Facilities and sections in public library.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find libraries in three cities with certain facilities. We need to call the function public_library_find_nearby for each location with appropriate facilities. The function expects location string and facilities which can be one of the enumerated values: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[].

We need to provide an array of facilities? The type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[], but that seems ambiguous. It might mean that facilities can be one of those strings or an array of "Cafe"? Actually "Cafe"[] indicates an array of "Cafe". But maybe they want to pass an array of strings? The function signature is ambiguous. But we can guess that we should pass an array of strings: e.g., ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

But the type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[], so maybe we need to pass a single string or an array of "Cafe"? That seems odd. But likely they want to pass an array of strings. Let's assume we pass an array of strings.

Thus we need to call the function three times:

1. location: "New York, NY", facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"]
2. location: "Los Angeles, CA", facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"]
3. location: "Chicago, IL", facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"]

We need to call the function for each. We'll produce separate calls.
